title: Seat quota consume() is inclusive of the limit and blocks only the (N+1)th user
description: entitlement/quota.service.js consume(orgId,'users',count) does an atomic findOneAndUpdate with $expr:{$lte:[{$add:[usage.users, count]}, limit]}. At usage.users===limit, adding 1 more must fail; reaching exactly limit must succeed.
preconditions: Org quota fixture with usage.users=9, limit.users=10
steps: Call quota.consume(orgId, 'users', 1) — expect success, usage.users becomes 10
Call quota.consume(orgId, 'users', 1) again with usage.users now at 10
Inspect the return value / thrown error
expectedResult: First call succeeds (10 <= 10). Second call throws QuotaExceededError since 10+1=11 > 10; no partial write occurs to usage.users on the failed attempt.

title: Seat quota check is skipped entirely when limit is -1 (unlimited) or org is project-billed
description: quota.service.js skips the $expr predicate when limit===-1. Separately, user.controller.js:372-381 only invokes quota.consume at all when isPricingV1Enabled(orgId) AND org.billingMode !== 'project' — project-billed orgs are fully exempt from org-level user quota.
steps: Call quota.consume(orgId, 'users', 5) for an org whose users limit is -1
Call the invite-user creation path for an org with billingMode='project' when usage.users already exceeds any nominal org-level cap
expectedResult: Both calls succeed with no quota rejection — limit=-1 never triggers the predicate, and project-billed orgs never call quota.consume for users at all.

title: Role pre('save') hook throws when an existing document has isSystem=true
description: role.model.js:44-49 pre('save') hook: if (!this.isNew && this.isSystem) throw a generic Error, independent of the controller-level 400 response. This is the last line of defense even if a controller path bypassed its own guard.
preconditions: An existing Role document with isSystem=true, systemRoleKey='SUPERADMIN'
steps: Load the SUPERADMIN Role document (isNew will be false)
Mutate a field (e.g. description) and call .save() directly on the Mongoose document, bypassing role.controller.js
expectedResult: The pre('save') hook throws before persistence; the document in the database is unchanged.

title: Resend-invite cooldown blocks a second call within 60 seconds of invitedAt
description: user.controller.js resendInvite (lines 738-781) computes RESEND_INVITE_COOLDOWN_MS=60000 against invitedAt. A call inside the window must return 409 without re-triggering the Keycloak invite email.
preconditions: A user with status='invited', keycloakUserId=null, invitedAt=Date.now()-30000 (30s ago)
steps: Call resendInvite(userId) 30 seconds after the original invite
Call resendInvite(userId) again 65 seconds after the original invite
expectedResult: First call is rejected with 409 'An invitation was just sent. Please wait a minute.' Second call (past the 60s window) succeeds and re-triggers the Keycloak invite.

title: gridToPermissions() maps none/view/edit/full + approve to the correct flat permission strings
description: featureAccessMap.js gridToPermissions/permissionsToGrid convert the persisted accessGrid (Mixed) into flat Role.permissions strings and back. VALID_LEVELS supports none|view|edit|full plus a separate approve boolean, even though AccessGrid.jsx's UI currently only offers 3 buttons (none/view/full).
steps: Call gridToPermissions({ evidence: { level: 'edit', approve: true } })
Feed the resulting permissions array back into permissionsToGrid()
expectedResult: gridToPermissions returns ['evidence.read','evidence.update','evidence.approve'] (no 'evidence.delete'/'evidence.admin' since level is 'edit' not 'full'). Round-tripping through permissionsToGrid reproduces { evidence: { level:'edit', approve:true } } exactly — no lossy collapse to 'view' or 'full'.

title: assertGrantablePermissions rejects a grant that exceeds the caller's own held permissions
description: Used identically in both user.controller.js (extraPermissions/role assignment) and role.controller.js (custom role create/update) to prevent privilege escalation: a caller can only grant permissions they themselves already hold.
expectedResult: Throws a 403 error listing 'organization.admin' as ungrantable; a structured log event 'authz.privilege_escalation.attempt' is emitted with the caller's id and the rejected permission.

title: validateRoleIds rejects a roleId that belongs to a different organization and is not a system role
description: user.controller.js validateRoleIds (lines 110-152), called from assignRoles, checks each roleId either has organizationId matching the caller's org OR is a system role (organizationId=null). A cross-org custom roleId must be rejected before it ever reaches Role assignment.
preconditions: roleId belongs to Org B's custom role, caller operates in Org A
expectedResult: Function throws/returns invalid before any User.roleIds write occurs; no cross-org role reference is ever persisted.
